job.title: Operations Planner
job.description: Night boats leave Tanjong basin after the last commuter ferry, and Harbor Kiln Transit needs an operations planner who can keep that schedule honest. You will sit with the duty master each afternoon, compare the tide window to the cargo list, and write the order in which barges take the inner berth. When a kiln load is late from Jurong, you will re-cut the night plan so the crew still finishes before the morning passenger run. The role owns the weekly berth chart, the overtime roster for the deck hands, and the short note that goes to the port office when a slot moves. You will also walk the quay twice a week with the safety lead and log any broken fender or dark lamp. We want someone who has planned shifts in a yard, a depot, or a small fleet, and who can explain a change to a coxswain without a slide deck. Spreadsheets are fine. A marine licence is useful but not required. The team is eight people. Apply through the careers page with a one-page note on a night you had to rebuild a plan after a delay. Harbor Kiln Transit pays monthly, lists the range in the portal, and never asks an applicant to buy a radio or a pass. Interviews are on site at the basin office.

job.title: Digital Collections Cataloguer
job.description: Dusty accession logs from the 1970s still sit in the mezzanine at Pine Quay Archives. We need a cataloguer who can turn those pages into records that a researcher can find without walking the stacks. You will photograph fragile ledgers under the copy stand, write a title and a date range for each volume, and attach the scan to the existing catalogue number. Some boxes hold parish newsletters. Others hold shipping lists from the old quay. You will not rewrite history; you will describe what is in the box and flag pages that need a conservator. Two mornings a week you will sit the reading-room desk and fetch requested items. The rest of the week is quiet bench work. We use a local Dublin Core profile and a simple spreadsheet for items that the database cannot hold yet. Experience with archives, a museum register, or a library special collection is enough. Fluency in English is required. Malay or Tamil helps with the older parish files. Pine Quay Archives is a small trust. The catalogue is public. Send a short sample record for any physical item you have described, plus the usual curriculum vitae, to collections@pinequayarchives.example. The trust does not charge applicants and does not hire through messaging apps.

note: Written legitimate archives role. Named trust, named catalogue duties, and a company mailbox. Purpose is a hire.

job.title: Studio Technician
job.description: Kilns cool overnight in the yard behind Marble Hill Ceramics, and the studio needs a technician who can read a pyrometer without guessing. You will load bisque and glaze firings, keep the two electric kilns on a written schedule, and mix the house glazes from the recipes on the wall. When a shelf warps, you will cut a new one and log the batch. The resident potters handle their own throwing. You handle the heat, the clay store, and the damp room. Once a month you will also open the studio for a public firing night: set the chairs, keep the walkway clear, and write a short card that names the clay body and the cone. We want someone who has fired a kiln in a school, a community studio, or a small shop. A ceramics diploma is welcome. So is a careful hand and a habit of writing down what you changed. Hours are Tuesday to Saturday, with one late Thursday for the public night. The clay store is locked and the key lives with the technician. Apply at the studio desk or by mail to studio@marblehillceramics.example with two photographs of firings you ran and a note on a firing that went wrong and how you recovered the load. Marble Hill Ceramics pays a monthly wage posted on the board by the sink. The studio issues the gloves and the respirator. Applicants do not buy a kiln shelf or a pyrometer as a condition of the offer.
